heading: Shared behavior annotations: all supported languages
body: Most Yon languages support 23 shared behavior annotations. The languages are JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, PHP, Java, Groovy, Kotlin, C#, Rust, Dart and Go. Tac supports the annotations in JavaScript, TypeScript and Dart browser services. It also supports them in native Swift, Kotlin, C# and Rust services and in Go web services. Swift is not a Yon language. Native ports have typed execution adapters, not an embedded JavaScript runtime. The names need no import in any language, because Tachyon annotations and types are global. JavaScript and TypeScript write @Name. Other languages use these forms: @Name for Java, Groovy, Kotlin, Swift and Dart; @snake_case for Python; [Name] for C#; #[Name] for PHP, Ruby and Rust. Rust also accepts the namespaced forms #[yon::snake_case] and #[tac::snake_case]. Go uses standalone // @Name comments, with one space after //. The comments are valid Go syntax and keep their spelling under gofmt (ADR 0050). The examples on this site leave out the package line, so add one, such as package main, before you run gofmt on a copied example. Type checking still needs the framework declarations that Tachyon generates. Put a marked Go parameter on its own line, followed by a comma. A comment marker that is close to a Tachyon name, such as // @GetRote, fails the build and suggests the right name. Other comments such as the // @Summary lines of swag stay ordinary comments. Run ty migrate fix --write to convert the old Go bracket markers. Ruby writes each marker as a #[Name] comment line, alone on its line, so an annotated Ruby file stays ordinary Ruby (ADR 0054). Ruby has every shared behavior annotation, in Yon and in Tac services. A parameter marker such as #[Check(ProductInput)] stands on its own line inside a parameter list written over several lines, and YARD tags give the types. Each marker is on its own line. Object options are strict JSON literals. You need no annotation package, no reflection scanner and no global decorator registration. A reflection scanner is code that inspects classes while the program runs. The Cache import is local to the source file. It does not replace the Cache constructor of the browser. Invalid declarations fail with TY1308.
